sentences.text: Bishanopliosaurus was a small plesiosaur that measured approximately 4 meters in length.
This animal can be distinguished from other species by the bifurcated ribs of its sacrum, a unique skeletal feature.
Fossil evidence suggests Bishanopliosaurus was unusually adapted to a freshwater environment, which is surprising for a marine reptile.
The genus Bishanopliosaurus was described by Dong in 1980.
The type species of the genus is Bishanopliosaurus youngi, serving as the primary reference for the group.
Remains of this creature have been found in the Ziliujing Formation in China.
Bishanopliosaurus is classified as a genus of plesiosaur, a group of marine reptiles.
It belongs to the parent group Rhomaleosauridae, making this family its immediate classification.
Within the broader tree of life, Bishanopliosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
A second species, B. zigongensis, was described by Gao et al. in 2003.
Bishanopliosaurus lived from the Toarcian to the Oxfordian stages, between 184.2 and 154.8 million years ago.
The second species, B. zigongensis, is known from the Xiashaximiao Formation, which is slightly later than the Ziliujing Formation.
